vocabulary.definition: used to introduce a surprising fact despite what was just mentioned
examples: She was tired; even so, she kept working.
It was raining; even so, they went for a walk.
The movie was long; even so, I enjoyed it.
He apologized; even so, she was still upset.
The task was difficult; even so, they managed to finish it.

vocabulary.definition: used to describe something that improves upon a previous situation or thing
examples: This cake is good, but the chocolate one is even better.
I thought the movie was great, but the sequel was even better.
She did well in her first performance, but her second one was even better.
The weather today is even better than yesterday.
Their new album is even better than the last one.

vocabulary.definition: used to describe something that is more negative than another thing
examples: The weather was bad yesterday, but today it's even worse.
I was late for the meeting, and even worse, I forgot my notes.
The situation is bad, but it could get even worse.
He failed the test, and even worse, he didn’t study at all.
The traffic is bad now, but during rush hour it gets even worse.
